name: Solomon Temple
description: A magnificent white marble temple built by Kohhran Thianghlim (The Holy Church) featuring a striking central dome and four corner towers. One of the largest churches in Mizoram, it can accommodate over 2,000 worshippers and offers panoramic views of Aizawl city.
how_to_reach: Located in Chawlhhmun, about 4 km from Aizawl city center. Accessible by taxi or local bus from Aizawl.
practical_notes: Open daily 6:00 AM to 8:00 PM. Photography allowed inside. Remove shoes before entering. Sunday services attract large crowds. Dress modestly.

name: Dzukou Valley
description: A stunning high-altitude valley straddling the Mizoram-Nagaland border at 2,452 meters. Famous for its seasonal carpets of dwarf bamboo and endemic Dzukou lily. The valley offers panoramic views of rolling hills and is a popular trekking destination.
how_to_reach: From Champhai town (65 km from Aizawl), hire a taxi to the trek base at Zokhawthar. The valley is reached via a moderate 5-6 hour trek from the border town.
practical_notes: Best visited March-June for flowers, October-March for clear views. Carry warm clothing, rain gear, and camping gear for overnight stays. No accommodation in the valley. Hire local guide. Permit required from Champhai DC office.

name: Rih Dil Lake
description: A heart-shaped natural lake near the Indo-Myanmar border, considered sacred in Mizo folklore. The crystal-clear waters reflect the surrounding hills and is believed to be the passage for departed souls. One of Mizoram's most picturesque natural landmarks.
how_to_reach: About 60 km from Champhai town. Accessible by road via Tiau River bridge. Hire a taxi or SUV from Champhai (2-3 hour drive on rough roads).
practical_notes: Best visited October-March. Inner Line Permit required for non-Mizoram residents. Carry food and water as no facilities nearby. Respect local beliefs - no swimming or littering. Mobile connectivity limited.
address: Near Tiau River, Champhai district, Mizoram

name: Murlen National Park
description: A 200 sq km national park near the Myanmar border, home to clouded leopards, hoolock gibbons, Himalayan black bears, and over 150 bird species. Features steep cliffs, dense tropical forests, and the famous Murlen cliff formations.
how_to_reach: About 245 km from Aizawl via Champhai. Hire SUV from Champhai (60 km, 3 hours on rough roads). Park entry from Rabung village.
practical_notes: Best visited November-March. Entry permit from Wildlife Warden, Aizawl required. Hire local guide. Basic forest rest house available (book in advance). No mobile connectivity. Carry supplies.
entry_fee: Entry permit required (Indian: nominal, Foreign: higher)
address: Near Rabung village, Champhai district, Mizoram

name: Vaphai Waterfall
description: A picturesque waterfall near Vaphai village cascading down steep cliffs into a natural pool. Surrounded by lush greenery and offers a refreshing stop during Champhai exploration.
how_to_reach: About 35 km from Champhai town. Accessible by road to Vaphai village, then short walk.
practical_notes: Best during monsoon (June-September) for full flow. Carry rain gear. Swimming possible in pool but exercise caution. No facilities nearby.

name: Hmunhmung Heritage Village
description: A traditional Mizo village preserving authentic architecture with thatched houses, zawlbuk (bachelor dormitory), and traditional granaries. Offers insight into pre-colonial Mizo lifestyle and customs.
how_to_reach: About 160 km from Aizawl via Hnahthial town. Hire taxi from Hnahthial (30 km, 1.5 hours).
practical_notes: Open daily 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM. Local guide recommended for cultural context. Respect village customs. Photography allowed with permission. Small entry fee supports village maintenance.

name: Kawlbem Waterfall
description: A multi-tiered waterfall cascading through dense forest, creating natural pools at each level. A hidden gem in Hnahthial district surrounded by pristine forest.
how_to_reach: About 40 km from Hnahthial town. Requires 4WD vehicle and short trek from nearest road point.
practical_notes: Best June-October. Moderate trek required. Carry water and snacks. No facilities. Hire local guide recommended.

name: Khawzawl Park & Viewpoint
description: A well-maintained park offering panoramic views of the surrounding hills and valleys. Features walking trails, a children's play area, and a viewpoint overlooking the Tuirial river valley.
how_to_reach: Located in Khawzawl town, about 152 km from Aizawl. Accessible by road from Aizawl (4-5 hours).
practical_notes: Open daily 6:00 AM to 7:00 PM. Best at sunrise/sunset for views. Free entry. Good for family outings. Basic facilities available.

name: Tiau River (Border River)
description: The natural border river between India and Myanmar, flowing through dramatic gorges. Offers stunning views of the international border and opportunities for riverside picnics and photography.
how_to_reach: Accessible from Khawzawl town via road to various border points (Zokhawthar, etc.).
practical_notes: Inner Line Permit required. Best November-March. Do not cross border. Photography of border posts restricted. Carry ID documents.

name: Khanmun Waterfall
description: A scenic waterfall near Kolasib town surrounded by bamboo groves. Popular local picnic spot with easy access and natural swimming pools.
how_to_reach: About 15 km from Kolasib town on Kolasib-Bairabi road. Accessible by taxi or local bus.
practical_notes: Best July-October. Easy access, good for families. Carry extra clothes for swimming. Small eateries nearby. Weekend crowds.

name: Tamdil Lake
description: A natural lake surrounded by hills and forests, known for boating and fishing. Name means 'Lake of Mustard' in Mizo. Surrounded by legend and surrounded by lush greenery.
how_to_reach: About 85 km from Aizawl, 10 km from Kolasib town. Well-connected by road.
practical_notes: Open daily 6:00 AM to 6:00 PM. Boating available (nominal fee). Fishing with permit. Lakeside restaurant available. Good for day trips from Aizawl.

name: Ngengpui Wildlife Sanctuary
description: A 110 sq km sanctuary in southern Mizoram protecting tropical evergreen forests. Home to elephants, tigers, hoolock gibbons, capped langurs, and diverse birdlife including hornbills.
how_to_reach: About 295 km from Aizawl via Lunglei. Requires full day journey. Hire SUV from Lawngtlai (60 km from sanctuary entrance).
practical_notes: Entry permit from Wildlife Warden required. Best November-March. Very remote - carry all supplies. Forest rest house at Ngengpui (book early). Hire local guide mandatory. No connectivity.

name: Saikao Village
description: A historic Mara tribal village known for its unique architecture and the historic Saikao Church built in 1924. Offers authentic Mara cultural experience and traditional hospitality.
how_to_reach: About 30 km from Lawngtlai town. Accessible by road.
practical_notes: Respect local customs and church timings. Homestays available (book in advance). Try traditional Mara cuisine. Buy local handicrafts.

name: Lunglei Town Viewpoint (Saikuti Hall)
description: Panoramic viewpoint offering sweeping views of Lunglei town spread across hills, the Mat river valley, and distant mountain ranges. Popular for sunset watching.
how_to_reach: Located in Lunglei town (165 km from Aizawl). Accessible by road (5-6 hours from Aizawl).
practical_notes: Best at sunset. Free access. Good photography spot. Combine with visit to Saikuti Hall cultural center.

name: Thorangtlang Wildlife Sanctuary
description: A 50 sq km sanctuary protecting bamboo forests and grasslands. Important corridor for elephants moving between India and Bangladesh. Home to barking deer, wild boar, and diverse avifauna.
how_to_reach: About 70 km from Lunglei town. Requires 4WD and local guide. Access via Thenzawl road.
practical_notes: Entry permit from Wildlife Warden, Lunglei. Best November-March. Very basic facilities. Hire local guide. No accommodation inside.

name: Pallel Heritage Site
description: Historic site with ancient monoliths and memorial stones commemorating Mizo chiefs and warriors. Provides insight into pre-Christian Mizo society and traditional leadership.
how_to_reach: About 20 km from Lunglei town on Lunglei-Thenzawl road.
practical_notes: Open daily. Local guide recommended for historical context. Respect the memorial stones. Photography allowed.

name: Dampa Tiger Reserve
description: Mizoram's largest protected area (500 sq km) and a Project Tiger reserve on the Bangladesh border. Protects tropical evergreen forests housing tigers, clouded leopards, elephants, hoolock gibbons, and over 250 bird species including the great hornbill.
how_to_reach: About 110 km from Aizawl via Mamit. Hire SUV from Mamit (25 km to park entrance at Phuldungsei).
practical_notes: Entry permit from Field Director, Dampa Tiger Reserve required. Best November-April. Forest rest houses at Teirei and Damparengpui (book well in advance). Hire authorized guide mandatory. No mobile connectivity inside.
entry_fee: Entry permit required (Indian: nominal, Foreign: higher)

name: Rwmzawm Tourist Spot
description: A scenic hilltop destination offering panoramic views of the surrounding valleys and the Dampa forest. Features a watchtower, walking trails, and picnic facilities.
how_to_reach: About 30 km from Mamit town. Accessible by road.
practical_notes: Best at sunrise. Watchtower climb involves stairs. Carry water and snacks. No facilities at top. Good for day trips from Aizawl.

name: Saitual Senate Viewpoint
description: Elevated viewpoint offering panoramic views of Saitual town, the Tuirial river valley, and surrounding hills. Popular for sunrise and sunset photography.
how_to_reach: Located in Saitual town, about 85 km from Aizawl. Well-connected by road.
practical_notes: Best at sunrise/sunset. Free access. Good for photography. Combine with Tamdil Lake visit.

name: Serchhip Lake (Vantawng Lake)
description: A serene artificial lake created by the Serchhip hydroelectric project. Surrounded by hills and forests, offers boating and peaceful lakeside walks.
how_to_reach: Located near Serchhip town, about 112 km from Aizawl. Well-connected by road.
practical_notes: Open daily 6:00 AM to 6:00 PM. Boating available. Lakeside walking path. Small cafe nearby. Good for family outings.
address: Near Serchhip town, Serchhip district, Mizoram

name: Vantawng Waterfall
description: Mizoram's highest waterfall at 229 meters, cascading in multiple tiers through dense forest. The 13th highest waterfall in India, surrounded by bamboo groves and creating a spectacular mist.
how_to_reach: About 135 km from Aizawl, 5 km from Thenzawl town. Well-marked road from Serchhip.
practical_notes: Best July-October for full flow. Viewing platform available. Monsoon can be slippery. No swimming. Small entry fee. Photography allowed.

name: Palak Lake (Pala Tipo)
description: Mizoram's largest natural lake (30 sq km) nestled in the hills near the Myanmar border. Rich in fish and birdlife, surrounded by pristine forest. Sacred in Mara folklore with legends of a submerged village.
how_to_reach: About 370 km from Aizawl via Lunglei. Full day journey. Hire SUV from Siaha (30 km from lake).
practical_notes: Best November-March. Inner Line Permit required. Boating with local fishermen. Lakeside camping possible (permission needed). Very remote - carry supplies. Homestays in nearby villages.

name: Siaha Town & Mara Culture
description: The headquarters of Mara Autonomous District Council, showcasing unique Mara tribal culture. Visit the Mara traditional house, local market, and historic churches. Gateway to Palak Lake.
how_to_reach: About 370 km from Aizawl. Daily bus service from Aizawl (10-12 hours).
practical_notes: Inner Line Permit required for non-residents. Try Mara cuisine (bamboo shoot dishes). Visit local market for handicrafts. Basic hotels available. Respect local customs.
